description: Pinned splits for KERNEL-SPEC §5's Largest Remainder Method. Weights and population sizes come from the shipped telco-payment-recovery example where the example declares them; every count below is computed by flux_engine.core.lrm, never typed. 'residualOrder' is the order keys stand in line for a residual unit -- largest fractional part first, ties by NFC-sorted key -- so a vector pins the tie-break itself and not only its effect.
regenerate: see the module docstring of tests/core/test_lrm.py

vectors.name: telco lifecycleMix over the declared population
vectors.note: world.flux.yml spec.population: size 25000, lifecycleMix {new, active, atrisk, churned}. Exact: no residual to place.

vectors.name: telco lifecycleMix over a population that does not divide
vectors.note: The same declared mix over 25001 subjects: one residual unit to place.

vectors.name: adversarial tie: experiment variants over an odd population
vectors.note: Both fractional parts are exactly 1/2. The tie is broken by NFC-sorted key, so the residual unit goes to 'control' -- never to a seed, and never to whichever variant was declared first.

vectors.name: adversarial tie: declaration order reversed
vectors.note: The same two variants declared the other way round. The counts are the same -- order-invariance -- and the output key order follows the input.

vectors.name: adversarial tie: two equal fractional parts, three keys
adversarial tie: every fractional part equal
vectors.note: Four keys at 0.25 over 10 units: floors 2 each, two residual units, all four fractional parts exactly 1/2. The first two NFC-sorted keys win.

vectors.name: adversarial tie: NFC decides, not code point
vectors.note: 'z' sorts before the composed 'e-acute' (U+00E9) and after the decomposed spelling (U+0065 U+0301). Sorting by NFC form rather than by raw code point is what makes the two spellings of the same key resolve one way.

vectors.name: declared scale is not significance
vectors.note: 0.150 and 0.15 are one number; a trailing declared zero must not move a count.

vectors.name: many keys, one unit
vectors.note: n = 1 over five equal shares: every floor is 0 and the single residual unit goes to the first NFC-sorted key.

vectors.name: a weight of zero receives nothing
long decimals inside the declared tolerance
vectors.note: Three shares that sum to 0.999999999 -- exactly at the 1e-9 tolerance KERNEL-SPEC §5 allows.
